chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Riyah Al-Qalla', who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man whose brother died and left a box containing some mortgage deposits (rhuun); upon some was the name of their owner and the amount they were mortgaged for, and upon some it was not known who they were for nor the amount they were mortgaged for. So what do you see regarding this one whose owner is not recognized? He said: 'It is like its entirety.'

key_terms.رُهُونٌ: Mortgage deposits or pledges held as security for a debt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on unclaimed mortgage deposits left in a deceased person's estate when the owner is unknown?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of unclaimed mortgage deposits (*rhuun*) found in a deceased's estate where the creditor and debt amount are unknown. He rules that such items are treated as the deceased's own property (*kamalihi*), meaning they become part of the general estate for distribution among heirs rather than being held in escrow or returned to the debtor. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of presuming ownership in the absence of specific evidence to the contrary, ensuring efficient estate settlement.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Muhammad Bin Rayah Al Qalla’a who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a man whose brother died and left a box wherein were some security deposits he had held. Upon some was the name of its owner, and with how much it had been mortgaged with, and some of these he did not know who it was for, nor with whom much it had been mortgaged with. So what is your view regarding this the owner of which is not recognised?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would be like his own wealth’.
en.sarwar: 19. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Riyah al-Qala’ who has said the following:

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man whose brother had died and left a box in which there were al-Rahn (security deposit) goods, of which certain ones had the name of the owner on them and others did not have any names on them and for how much they were left as al- Rahn (security deposit), and what do you say about that with an unknown owner. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is like his own property.’”
